author: Joseph Garcia
policy: Use the maintainer's answers as page copy. Questions stay in this private editorial record and are never displayed on the website. Preserve wording; paragraph breaks, HTML escaping and relevant links are allowed. Ask before substantive shortening or rewriting. Existing unanswered copy is not approved just because it is already present.

sections.question: Imagine someone has just found Homegames and knows nothing about it: how would you describe what it is, who you made it for, and what you hope they get out of it?
sections.answer: Homegames is a free and open source platform that lets you play, make and share games without an account.

sections.question: What do you want someone to know about making or changing a game with Homegames? Explain what they can do and why you think it's worth trying, in the words you'd want on the page.
sections.answer: Develop and preview your game in the browser and share it with friends when you're ready
sections.notes: Replaces the previous introductory sentence and generated feature bullet list. Screenshot and action links remain.

sections.question: Why would someone want to run Homegames on their own computer, and who is that option for? The download and setup links can handle the technical steps.
sections.answer: Running Homegames yourself gives you a dedicated game server easily joinable by people on your network via homegames.link
sections.notes: homegames.link is linked without changing the text. Live discovery and native release acceptance remain deployment gates.

sections.question: How would you introduce yourself as the person behind the project, and what does Homegames mean to you? We'll use the About page afterward for the fuller story.
sections.answer: Homegames has gone through several phases over almost a decade of development. The goal has always been to make it easy for people to play and share simple games. At the moment, I think Homegames is in the most sustainable and solid place it's ever been and I think in some way that original goal has been achieved.

sections.question: How did Homegames begin, and what changed across those phases to bring it to the version you're releasing now?
sections.answer: The original inspiration for Homegames was Jackbox. "Easily joinable social games from your phone that you play with people in your house" was the goal at the start. After iterating on that idea over time, I ended up with user accounts, asset uploads, a searchable public catalog people could publish their own games to, and a lot more. It became unmanageable at a certain point, and ultimately I am not interested in hosting a service and dealing with all of the responsibility and costs of doing that. If the ultimate idea is to provide a useful tool to people for free, I want to reduce the dependence on me and the services I provide to keep this idea going. That is what led to the mostly P2P structure we have today, with a free hosted option available to people if they want.
sections.clarification: The maintainer clarified that free hosted option refers to the self-hosted server bundle/dashboard. Others may also host their own website or public server. Applied wording: a free self-hosted server bundle available to people if they want.

sections.question: Why does it matter to you that people can keep, change and share their games, and what do you want that to mean for someone using Homegames?
sections.answer: I don't want games to depend on homegames infrastructure or services. Providing downloadable game bundles playable offline in your browser and access to the source code makes the game last longer.
sections.notes: Source code is linked without changing the wording. The separate factual license notice remains.

sections.question: What would you like people to get in touch about, and how would you like them to participate in Homegames?
sections.answer: Ask questions or give me feedback on the platform, games or anything else Homegames related

gameSections.question: Keep one chosen speaker, or let each person enable sound on their own device?
gameSections.answer: Let each person enable sound
